lessons.lesson: When the conductor rewrote the decisions entry 'What the work is for' after the feedback, it wrote into the entry how the decision was reached ('asked for as new contributors and confirmed at the plan sign-off feedback'). turn carried that into G1, so the plan broke B-6 and had to be made a second time. The entry should hold only what is decided. How it was reached already lives in the commit message, which said it in its 'Answer:' line. Nothing in rn's steps told the conductor to keep the history out of a decisions entry, which is why the same slip can happen in anyone's session.

grounds.quote: new=\"## What the work is for\\n\\nThe README greets new contributors and points them to the CONTRIBUTING file, so someone who comes to contribute knows where to start; asked for as new contributors and confirmed at the plan sign-off feedback.\\n\"
Keep turn's plan and have it made again: G1 said how it was reached, which the decisions and commits keep (B-6)
Answer: the point behind it was who the greeting is for; the request said new contributors, which had been widened to newcomers unasked.

lessons.lesson: The plan sign-off was shown to the user in English, even though the conversation language is Japanese. The conductor showed what `rn.py proposal plan` printed as it was. That text is also the sign-off commit message, so it is in the artifact language. The skill tells the conductor both to use what rn.py prints as printed and to say everything to the user in the conversation language, and at a sign-off these two rules clash. rn should give the conductor the proposal in the conversation language for the user, separate from the commit message, or tell it to translate the proposal before showing it.

grounds.quote:

Everything you say to the user is in the state's
`conversation-language`, everything you write to the repository, such as a commit message, in its
`artifact-language`.

lessons.lesson: turn's result cited steering.md:1, a front-matter line, as the Good for every plan item on both runs. Its own 'checked' said 'no run: a stand-in'. rn's step says such a result goes back to turn, but turn would return the same result every time, and rn's steps give no way out of that loop. The conductor had to make up a way on: it checked lines 11, 15 and 16 itself and asked the user whether its own check could stand. So the plan reached the sign-off with no check by a second AI. rn's steps should say what the conductor does when turn's result cannot give the Good it claims and making the work again would not change that.
